attributes.title: Detection header
attributes.visState:
{"title": "Detection header", "type": "markdown", "params": {"fontSize": 12, "openLinksInNewTab": false, "markdown": "### Detection — live alerts & anomalies
An **alert** is a hard rule that crossed a fixed threshold — someone decided in advance what "too much" means. An **anomaly** is a time window that a learned model scored as unlike this host's own recent normal; the *grade* is how unusual (0–1) and the *confidence* is how much history the model had to judge it on. A high grade at low confidence is a young model, not an emergency.

The tables summarise; the two panels beneath them list the individual records with their timestamps. All of it is pinned to the last hour and ignores the time picker.

*Where* is the host or collector the model was watching. Some detectors watch the cluster as one stream and have no host — those read **whole fleet**, and the host counter to the left deliberately does not count them."}, "aggs": []}

attributes.title: Act on this
attributes.visState:
{"title": "Act on this", "type": "markdown", "params": {"fontSize": 12, "openLinksInNewTab": false, "markdown": "### ⚙️ Act on this
This dashboard is read-only. To acknowledge, mute or edit a rule:

**[Alerts →](/app/alerting#/dashboard)** — acknowledge an alert so it stops counting as active.

**[Monitors →](/app/alerting#/monitors)** — change a threshold, or disable a rule that is crying wolf.

**[Anomaly detectors →](/app/anomaly-detection-dashboards#/detectors)** — per-detector history, the feature values behind a grade, and initialisation state.

Acknowledging is not the same as fixing: the rule will fire again on the next window that still breaches it."}, "aggs": []}

attributes.title: Incidents header
attributes.visState:
{"title": "Incidents header", "type": "markdown", "params": {"fontSize": 12, "openLinksInNewTab": false, "markdown": "### 🎯 Incidents — the headline
An **incident** is one episode: the signals that share a cause, counted and named. It is the record, not the notification — Alertmanager decides when to tell someone, `alice-incidents` decides what is true.

Grouping never destroys a signal. Every raw alert and anomaly behind an incident is still a row in `alice-signals`, in the panel below, with the `incident_id` that ties it back here.

`unknown-mass-silence` means the fleet went quiet and nothing authoritative said a run ended. It pages on purpose."}, "aggs": []}
